user_message: A friend told me I can pay for my flight after I take it instead of upfront — is that something I'd qualify for?
expected_answer_summary: Pay-per-invoice eligibility — the customer must be over 18 and a resident of Switzerland or the Principality of Liechtenstein, and the option is only available for flights departing from Switzerland. The agent should ask follow-up qualifying questions (age, residence, route) rather than make assumptions.

rubric.factual_correctness: Response correctly identifies the three eligibility requirements (18+, CH/LI resident, flights from Switzerland) and does not invent additional ones.
rubric.citation_accuracy: Response cites the pay-per-invoice section of the FAQ.
rubric.no_fabrication: Response does not invent eligibility criteria, fees, or payment terms beyond what the corpus states.

user_message: I'm filing my taxes and need to submit a receipt for my flight as a business expense. Do I need to ask you for a special invoice, or does the booking confirmation work?
expected_answer_summary: The e-ticket / booking confirmation is internationally recognised as a receipt in most countries (including Switzerland) and is sufficient for tax-return submission and business-expense reimbursement. A separately-issued special invoice is only available on request for flights originating in Greece, India, Italy, or Spain where the e-ticket may not meet local requirements. The agent should surface both facts even though the customer didn't volunteer their country, and should not invent additional jurisdictions or extra steps.

rubric.factual_correctness: Response correctly states that the e-ticket / booking confirmation is internationally recognised as a receipt usable for tax-return / business-expense purposes, and identifies the four special-jurisdiction countries (Greece, India, Italy, Spain) as the only exception.
rubric.citation_accuracy: Response cites the 'Ordering an invoice' section of the FAQ.
rubric.no_fabrication: Response does not invent additional special-jurisdiction countries beyond the four named, nor extra form names, fees, or processing times not present in the corpus.

user_message: Quick question before I check out — does paying by credit card cost more than other methods?
expected_answer_summary: The corpus addresses only the bank side of this question: some banks may charge additional fees in individual cases, and SWISS has no influence over those charges. The corpus does NOT explicitly state whether SWISS itself adds a credit-card-specific surcharge — a corpus-faithful agent surfaces the bank-fee caveat and does not invent a definitive SWISS-side claim in either direction.

rubric.factual_correctness: Response surfaces the bank-side caveat (some banks may charge additional fees in individual cases; SWISS has no influence over those charges). Does not assert as fact any claim the corpus does not make — including 'SWISS does not surcharge credit cards' (that is an inference from the section's framing, not a corpus statement).
rubric.citation_accuracy: Response cites the 'Frequently asked questions: Payment' section of the FAQ.
rubric.no_fabrication: Response does not invent specific surcharge percentages, named third-party processors, or fees not present in the corpus. Confident assertions about SWISS's own credit-card pricing not supported by the corpus are scored as fabrication.

user_message: Doing my expense report and I can't find the receipt for booking 002E3A. Can you tell me what I paid in total?
expected_answer_summary: The agent looks up booking 002E3A and reports the total amount on the booking row (393000 in the database's units; the schema does not annotate currency, so reporting the raw number or interpreting it as CHF cents (CHF 3,930.00) or CHF major units (CHF 393,000) are all factually correct). No corpus citation needed — this is purely a booking-data lookup.

rubric.factual_correctness: Response reports the total_amount from booking 002E3A. Accepts the raw value 393000 or any reasonable currency-unit interpretation (CHF 3,930.00 / CHF 393,000) — the database schema does not annotate currency, so the interpretation is downstream of the lookup. Reporting a different number is factually wrong.
rubric.citation_accuracy: Response does not fabricate corpus citations. The answer comes from booking data, not from swiss_faq.md; citing a FAQ section here is a fabrication.
rubric.no_fabrication: Response does not invent additional booking details (passenger names, ticket numbers, individual segment fares) that the customer did not ask about and that would require unprompted extra tool calls. Does not invent payment-method, refund-status, or other fields not in the bookings row.

user_message: Quick check — did my LX0086 leg on booking 3F0481 land OK? Trying to figure out if my next connection is going to work.
expected_answer_summary: The agent resolves booking 3F0481's itinerary, identifies the LX0086 segment (flight_id 11472, the unique LX0086 instance in this booking — flight_no alone is ambiguous across 61 rows), and reports status='Arrived'. May surface actual_departure / actual_arrival to address the connection-timing concern. Should not pull status for a different LX0086 instance not on this booking.

rubric.factual_correctness: Response reports status='Arrived' for the LX0086 instance on booking 3F0481 (flight_id 11472). Reporting a different status (or status of a different LX0086 flight instance not on this booking) is factually wrong. Surfacing actual_departure / actual_arrival times is a plus but not required.
rubric.citation_accuracy: Response does not fabricate corpus citations. Flight status comes from booking + flight data, not from swiss_faq.md.
rubric.no_fabrication: Response does not invent gate numbers, baggage carousel info, weather details, or onward-connection viability claims not derivable from the available tool outputs. Does not assert what the next connection is unless the agent actually inspected the rest of the itinerary.

user_message: Got an email about an upgrade offer for ticket 7240005435767874 on booking 0002D8 — what class am I currently flying?
expected_answer_summary: The agent calls get_booking_status('0002D8'), which returns the booking's itinerary including ticket 7240005435767874 and its segment fares. Both segments of that ticket (LX0136, CX0047) are Economy, so the answer is 'Economy' (uniform across the ticket's itinerary). The agent should not infer or invent upgrade eligibility — the customer asked only what class they are currently in. Note: the shared transactional tool surface is booking-keyed (get_booking_status takes booking_id; there is no get_ticket); the customer provided both the ticket and the booking, which is the natural phrasing for an upgrade-email scenario.

rubric.factual_correctness: Response reports fare_conditions='Economy' for ticket 7240005435767874 (both segments) after resolving via booking 0002D8. Reporting a different fare class is factually wrong.
rubric.citation_accuracy: Response does not fabricate corpus citations. Fare class comes from booking/ticket data, not from swiss_faq.md. Citing a corpus section about Economy fare conditions is over-answering — the customer asked what class they're in, not what the class entails.
rubric.no_fabrication: Response does not invent upgrade eligibility, upgrade pricing, or fare-rule details. Does not assert there is or isn't an upgrade path unless that information was actually retrieved (which the available tools do not surface).
